description: CanMV K230D AI-CAM (Kendryte K230D, 128 MB LPDDR4 in the package, a GC2093 camera, Wi-Fi), with its lens as a variant (72 or 140 degrees). 'AI-CAM' is a third-party name: Canaan's SDK calls the board 'K230D CanMV Junroc AI Cam'. It is not the BPI K230D Zero. A board record: Atlas flashes it from the K230 boot ROM's USB mode with Canaan's burner U-Boot and no vendor tool. Written from Canaan's SDK sources; untested on this board.

camera.source: k230_linux_sdk buildroot-overlay/linux/0024-add-junroc-board.patch (the kernel device tree) and the defconfig

ports: USB-C, USB0 in OTG mode (the one USB port the device tree enables)
second USB-C: UNCONFIRMED (presumed UART0 through a CH342K)
power input: UNCONFIRMED (the K230D Zero takes a USB-C 5 V 2 A supply; this board's is not sourced)
USB1: commented out in the device tree

storage_target_evidence: The SDK's device tree and U-Boot DTS (k230_linux_sdk): microSD on SDIO1 (mmc_sd1) holds the boot and the data; no eMMC; the OSPI/QSPI pins (GPIO14 to GPIO25) are not populated, so no SPI-NAND by default.
The K230 boot ROM enters USB download mode when its storage holds nothing it can boot (Canaan's burntool guide).
instructions: Put a blank (or unbootable) microSD card in the board: the boot ROM waits for USB only when it finds nothing to boot. Or hold the BOOT button (SW2, BOOT0 on GPIO1) while you power the board on.
Connect the board's USB-C port (USB0, OTG) to this computer with a data cable, and power the board (the power input is UNCONFIRMED: see todo).
The board appears as 29f1:0230 (K230 USB boot). Atlas loads Canaan's burner into it, writes the image to the microSD card, reads it back and restarts the board.
todo: The name: 'AI-CAM' is third-party. Canaan's SDK calls the board 'K230D CanMV Junroc AI Cam' (k230_linux_sdk buildroot-overlay/linux/0024-add-junroc-board.patch); MicroPython calls it 'CanMV K230D JUNROC_AI_CAM'. It is not the BPI K230D Zero (record bpi-canmv-k230d-zero).
29f1:0230 is the K230 boot ROM's id (kburn.h:205-206), the same id as the K230D Zero. A device in USB boot is offered as both (possible_models) until the board's burner or identity says which.

UNCONFIRMED: lens-72 (72 degree) has no source at all. UNCONFIRMED: lens-140 (140 degree) rests on one reseller listing for a 140-degree GC2093 module, not a vendor source. Check the module's label and the FPC pinout on the board.
UNCONFIRMED: which USB-C is the power input and which is UART0 (the second USB-C is presumed UART0 through a CH342K), and the supply's rating.

UNCONFIRMED: the burner file name. Canaan's burntool guide says the generated u-boot.bin is loader.bin, and the K230D Zero's Gaia build ships loader_mmc.bin, so both names are listed. Gaia needs: the burner (loader_mmc.bin or loader.bin, from the SDK's U-Boot for this board) and sdcard.img. There is no Gaia board config for the AI-CAM yet.

UNCONFIRMED: the load address. The record uses 0x80360000 (the tools' default, kburn_k230.h:31). The burner links at 0x80300000 (kendryte/k230_sdk); if it won't start at 0x80360000, set 0x80300000, as the K230D Zero record's todo says. Plug-in check: the set-data-address line in the trace.
The device tree names the GC2093; the RTOS defconfig also enables an OV5647 driver, which is not evidence that a module carries that sensor. Check the sensor on the board.
UNCONFIRMED: no LED, fan or header pins are sourced for this board.
The Wi-Fi (RTL8189FTV) needs a Gaia image with its driver and firmware; until one exists, board-lite has no address to answer on.
